notable_absence.predicate: providesService / requiresMinimumNodeCount / enablesIndependentDeploymentOf / triggersRebalance / requiresMemoryQuota / exemptFromMemoryQuota / hasInternalServiceIdentifier
notable_absence.finding: Seven predicates minted on one page - by far the highest mint rate of any round to date - and the reason is systematic, not accidental. The registry's 64 existing predicates are almost entirely about GATING (requiresPrivilege, requiresEdition, requiresCapellaRole, incompatibleWith*, availableSince): 'under what conditions may this construct be used'. That is the only question a syntax-reference or REST-reference page ever answers. This page answers a different family of questions entirely - what the product CONSISTS OF (catalog membership), how many of a thing must EXIST (minimum node count), what RESOURCES a component claims (memory quota), what an operation CAUSES (rebalance), and how a display name maps to a wire identifier. The registry has essentially no composition, cardinality, resource or causation vocabulary at all. dependsOnService (recurrence 3) is the single existing predicate in the composition family, and it was itself minted on this same learn/services-and-indexes subtree in round 1 - i.e. every composition predicate the ontology has came from the only conceptual pages it had ever seen. The hypothesis the round set out to test is confirmed strongly. Additionally: no predicate exists for OPTIONAL or ALTERNATIVE dependency (see query-service.json), and none for cardinality/arity constraints (see index-service.json).

cross_component_finding: Four separate issues on this one page. (1) DIRECT CONTRADICTION with indexes.md, one directory away: this page says the Index Service 'Creates indexes, for use by the Query and Analytics services', while indexes.md says 'The [Search](../services/search-service.md) and [Analytics Services](../services/analytics-service.md) create and use their own indexes' and 'The [Analytics Service](../services/analytics-service.md) provides analytics indexes for shadow data in an Analytics collection'. One of these is wrong. I recorded the servesService relation as this page states it rather than quietly dropping it, so reconciliation can see both sides. (2) ARBITER vs SERVICELESS NODE: paragraph 3 introduces arbiter nodes at 'Couchbase Server 7.6 and later versions'; the 'Setting Up Services' section separately introduces 'you can configure a node to run no services' at 'Couchbase Enterprise Server 7.6 and later'. Same release, adjacent capabilities, plausibly the same underlying mechanism, but the page never says so - and only the second is edition-gated. I minted two concepts rather than merge them, per the no-merging-without-a-source-statement rule, but an SME should confirm whether these are one feature or two. (3) EDITION WORDING: 'Couchbase Enterprise Server 7.6' is not the house style used everywhere else in the corpus ('Couchbase Server Enterprise Edition', as on index-service.md in the same directory). Worth a style fix; more importantly it made the requiresEdition extraction a judgement call rather than a lift. (4) The service list in 'Services and Multi-Dimensional Scaling' is a one-line paraphrase of each service page's own lede. data-service.md/query-service.md/index-service.md restate it, so a fact stated four times can drift in four places - and per (1) it already has.
cross_product_finding: This page has no Capella counterpart in the corpus, and that is itself the finding. Multi-Dimensional Scaling is the load-bearing concept here - services as independently placeable, independently quota'd, independently scalable components on named nodes - and Capella's management-plane pages (rounds 6-9, ~180 pages) never expose it: they expose cluster configurations, node counts and service checkboxes, with placement decided for you. The registry's Capella-derived concepts (capella:cluster-manager, cluster-access-credential-type, capella-role:*) have no server:node, server:rebalance or server:service-memory-quota to attach to, and nothing in the Capella tree needed them. So the ontology currently has two disjoint views of the same services - server/ sees deployable components with topology, Capella sees a managed feature list - joined only by the shared service:* ids. Note also that capella:cluster-manager and capella:xdcr are recorded as monitored components 'explicitly NOT one of the Services'; this page's closed seven-member catalog is the server/-side evidence that confirms that exclusion is real and not a Capella quirk (neither Cluster Manager nor XDCR appears in it).
